newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Komercni lowers reference rate to 17.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech Komercni lowers reference rate to 17.6 pct.

text.p: Komercni Banka a.s., the Czech republic's largest commercial bank, said on Wednesday that it would lower its reference lending rate by one full percentage point to 17.6 percent, effective July 3.
The bank added in a statement that it saw the current downtrend for interest rates on the local market continuing at least in the near future.
"Komercni Banka assumes that the declining trend of interest rates will continue further," Komercni said in a statement.
The statement added that Komercni's base lending rate for credits incurred before July 24, 1995 would fall to 15.7 percent, from a previous 16.5 percent.
Czech interest rates skyrocketed in mid-May when the central bank tightened its grip on the market in an attempt to save the crown from a wave of speculative short-selling.
The central bank hiked its main interest rates and cut off market liquidity, pushing interbank rates as high as 200 percent, before it was forced to freely float the crown on May 27.
Since then, rates have come down with the central bank's Lombard rate currently sitting at 23 percent after rising as high as 50 percent.
